The stated cause is Go build leftovers exceeding the ordinary 128 MiB inventory. R1 supplies a separate bounded cleanup before that inventory; R2 is enforced with no-follow directory opens; R3 is enforced with held descriptors, identity comparisons and unlink confirmation. Recursive removal reuses the same confirmation helper. No structural facts requiring individual mappings were listed in this brief.

Reviewed the declared artifacts and reconciled the explicit sealed range. Changes remain cohesive around Go leftover cleanup, its regressions and platform validation. The ordinary runtime byte budget is unchanged.

Examined descriptor-relative traversal, no-follow/nonblocking opens, identity checks, close-on-exec, bounded recursion and external-target preservation. No new external authority, dependency or sensitive logging was introduced.

Compared the implementation with increasing the general budget or using unrestricted recursive removal. The separate bounded inventory addresses the actual cause while preserving the existing budget and replacement checks. The helper is narrowly scoped. A Windows delivery requirement would invalidate the current fallback and require the documented F3 implementation.
